item.title: China rolls out "token factories" to drive AI economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
This photo provided by iSoftStone Information Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. shows a scene inside a token factory at the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 21, 2026. (Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- As AI applications gain momentum, China is accelerating the rollout of "token factories" in a bid to build an economic order suited to the AI era. Every time a user prompts an AI model to generate code, images or video, tokens are consumed behind the scenes. In March, China adopted "ciyuan" as the official Chinese term for "token," giving its AI services a standard unit for measuring, settling and tracking usage -- similar to how electricity is measured in kilowatt-hours. In late September, Beijing unveiled an action plan to accelerate the development of the token economy for 2026-2028. "This is the first provincial-level policy in China specifically dedicated to the token economy," said Zhang Jinrui, an official with the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology. "With the rollout of Beijing's new policy, tokens are no longer just a technical term associated with large models. The token economy has officially entered a stage of industrial application and institutional development," said Liu Yong, president of the Beijing-based Zhongguancun Internet Finance Institute. The Beijing action plan calls for building world-class token factories and establishing tiered evaluation standards, with throughput capacity, time to first token, PUE (power usage effectiveness) and cache hit rate as core metrics, to ensure the large-scale supply of high-quality tokens. A token factory can be thought of as the AI era's equivalent of a power plant. It integrates electricity, chips, data and models to directly produce tokens. Unlike traditional data centers that only rent out computing cards, customers no longer need to deploy models or optimize inference themselves -- they simply pay for the tokens they use. In the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, the Chinese capital's first token factory is now in operation, with a daily capacity of up to 1.4 trillion tokens in its first phase. The plan also designates token distribution platforms as part of the city's new infrastructure layout, exploring market-based pricing and circulation mechanisms for tokens, so that tokens can truly be measured and traded as an economic factor. On the application side, the new policy encourages the development of general-purpose and industry-specific AI agents, bringing token capabilities into sectors such as industry, research and government affairs. Chen Guangming, an official with the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology, said token consumption is currently growing fastest in AI-generated content and programming, and more vertical industries will become potential growth drivers for token consumption in the future. "In the internet era, competition was all about traffic and user attention. In the AI era, the logic has shifted -- what matters now is the quality and efficiency of outputting effective tokens," Liu said, adding that the shift from a traffic economy -- one built on user visits and attention -- to a token economy represents a new trend in China's economic development. Data from China's National Data Administration shows that by June, the country's average daily token calls had surpassed 500 trillion. "More than half of those calls were made in Beijing," Zhang said, noting that the city has so far registered 242 large models for public use. Beijing's early push is aimed not merely at building a series of token factories, but at exploring institutional rules suited to the token economy, making the city a testing ground for the industry's development, according to local authorities. Elsewhere, localities across China are developing token economies tailored to their own strengths, as part of efforts to implement the State Council's guidelines on the "AI Plus" initiative. The guidelines aim to build a systematic support framework for AI covering models, data, computing power, applications, open-source development, talent, policies and regulations, and security. In May, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, drawing on its green computing resources, launched a token trading platform integrating model calls, token matching and transaction settlement. Nanning, capital of south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, is exploring new models such as cross-border data compliance and remote model inference delivery, helping domestic computing power and large-model capabilities reach ASEAN markets as standardized token services. East China's Anhui Province, meanwhile, encourages banks to offer "token loans" as a financial tool for the token economy. Industry observers generally agree that the global token economy remains in its early stage but holds vast potential. A research report by CICC, a Chinese investment bank, sees "token factories" as one of the fastest-growing and most commercially promising business models for large-model developers in the near term. JPMorgan predicts that China's AI inference token consumption will grow about 370-fold between 2025 and 2030. China's three major telecom operators rolled out token packages in May for individual users as well as government and enterprise clients, bringing token commercialization further into reach for individual consumers. Li Lingran, an engineer at an internet company in Beijing, says using large AI models at work has become as essential as water. He now spends more than 200 yuan (about 30 U.S. dollars) a month on tokens, even more than his traditional mobile phone bill. "This is a shift you can't ignore," he said. ■ This photo provided by iSoftStone Information Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. shows a scene inside a token factory at the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 21, 2026. (Xinhua)

item.title: Global vine, wine congress kicks off in northwest China's Ningxia
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
This photo taken on Oct. 12, 2026 shows an exterior view of the venue of the opening ceremony of the 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Wang Peng) YINCHUAN, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- The 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine opened on Monday in Yinchuan, capital of northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China's top wine-producing area. This is the first time the congress, held alongside the 24th General Assembly of the International Organization of Vine and Wine (OIV), has been hosted in Asia since its launch in 1924. The event has drawn more than 800 participants, including delegates from 51 OIV member states, diplomatic envoys to China from 25 countries, representatives from 47 countries and international organizations, leading experts and scholars in the wine sector from at home and abroad, as well as heads of domestic business associations and leading enterprises. Themed around building a new landscape for the global vine and wine industry, the congress features an opening ceremony, a seminar on high-quality development of the Chinese vine and wine industry, a sci-tech sub-session, industry visits and a closing ceremony. Over 400 academic papers from 35 countries will be showcased at the sci-tech sub-session, introducing cutting-edge global wine technologies and helping drive the transformation and upgrading of China's vine and wine industry. The 6th China (Ningxia) International Wine Culture and Tourism Expo opened alongside the congress, attracting 84 world-renowned wineries and enterprises from distinctive production areas in 16 countries. It has also drawn a total of 146 leading domestic wineries from Ningxia and other core production areas in China. The eastern foot of Helan Mountain in Ningxia has become China's largest contiguous wine grape production area. This region has 607,000 mu, or about 40,467 hectares, dedicated to wine grape cultivation and development, accounting for nearly 42 percent of China's total. Ningxia, home to 261 wine enterprises, including 130 wineries, produces 140 million bottles of wine annually. The local wine industry has also become a driver of tourism. Wineries in Ningxia receive more than 3.7 million tourist visits each year, generating combined benefits of over 50 billion yuan (around 7.4 billion U.S. dollars). ■ This photo taken on Oct. 12, 2026 shows the opening ceremony of the 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine held in Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Wang Peng) A foreign guest learns about Ningxia's wine during the opening ceremony of the 47th World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Oct. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Peng)

item.title: Extended holiday boosts Chinese travel demand across Europe
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
* According to Trip.com Group data, 62 percent of Europe-bound flight bookings from Sept. 25 to Oct. 7 were for departures before Sept. 30. The average stay in Europe increased from 14.8 days in 2025 to 16.1 days. * Tour guide Zhang Hongbo in Barcelona has noticed that Chinese visitors are increasingly willing to spend on quality restaurants, attentive service and admission to historic buildings they might once have viewed only from outside. * Aviation consultancy CAPA said in an April analysis that capacity between China and Western Europe had surpassed 2019 levels, driven by Chinese airlines. WARSAW, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- For Chinese tourist Zou Yini and her friends, some of the greatest pleasures of their National Day holiday in Europe came from strolling through Barcelona's neighborhoods, browsing shops, and sampling local cuisine. After visiting France, the three continued to the Spanish city, where they spent several days exploring its culture and relishing its laid-back atmosphere. In China, this year's travel window combined two holidays separated by three days: the Mid-Autumn Festival from Sept. 25 to 27, and the National Day holiday from Oct. 1 to 7, giving ambitious travelers a possible 13-day getaway. The extended travel period fueled greater demand for long-haul trips to Europe, with some countries welcoming more visitors than last year and new opportunities for businesses across the continent. LONGER HOLIDAYS, WIDER HORIZONS For European tourism businesses, this year's holiday travel season began before Oct. 1, the first day of China's seven-day National Day holiday or Golden Week, as Chinese visitors set off earlier and stayed longer. According to Trip.com Group data, 62 percent of Europe-bound flight bookings from Sept. 25 to Oct. 7 were for departures before Sept. 30. The average stay in Europe increased from 14.8 days in 2025 to 16.1 days. The longer holiday period brought fresh business opportunities. In Italy, hotel bookings by Chinese travelers more than doubled year on year during the period, while flight bookings rose more than 40 percent, according to Italy's tourism industry federation Federturismo, citing Trip.com Group data. Interest also extended to destinations in Italy such as Bolzano, Sorrento and the Dolomites, giving travelers opportunities to combine visits to major cities with mountain scenery and regional attractions. France saw a similar demand. Citing Trip.com data, Tourism publication L'Echo touristique reported in September that hotel bookings in France by Chinese mainland travelers from Oct. 1 to 7, also known as the Golden Week, increased 129 percent year on year. Paris remained the main draw, with bookings up 132 percent, but the 15 most-booked destinations outside the capital posted average growth of 123 percent. They included Chamonix, Lyon, Strasbourg, Marseille, Bordeaux and Nice. Demand was also strong for organized tours. Shanghai-based Spring Tour said its Golden Week packages covering Spain and Portugal, the Balkans, Northern Europe and Greece had sold out by mid-August. A representative of the Association of Chinese Tour Guides in Hungary said seven-day tours linking Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Austria sold out by late August. BEYOND LANDMARKS The changing pattern of Chinese travel is also reflected in how visitors spend their time and money. In Paris, Chinese tourist Zhang Wen visited the Louvre, but another experience offered a different perspective on the city: a musical walk through Montmartre. Singer and guide Anne-Sophie Guerrier brought the neighborhood's musical history to life through songs and stories at the former homes and performance venues of French singers, and provided a Chinese-language guidebook for Chinese visitors. "The combination of live performances, stories and the neighborhood's historic atmosphere made the experience lively, romantic and memorable," Zhang said. "It offered me a different way to discover the culture and history of Paris." Tour guide Zhang Hongbo in Barcelona has noticed that Chinese visitors are increasingly willing to spend on quality restaurants, attentive service and admission to historic buildings they might once have viewed only from outside. "Now a lot of people want to know more about Spanish culture: how people live, how they have fun, how they eat," he said. In Switzerland, Chinese visitors are seeking a different kind of experience. A Shanghai tourist surnamed Zhao spent several days exploring the mountains in the Jungfrau region. Immersing himself in nature mattered more than simply visiting a long list of attractions. Tourism providers are adapting to these changing preferences. Oliver Hammel, CEO of Jungfrau Railways, said large Chinese tour groups had increasingly given way to smaller groups since the pandemic, while independent travel had also grown. Many independent visitors now use travel passes to explore multiple attractions across the region. In the Balkans, tour operator Yang Xiaoliang said his company served 329 Chinese visitors in 64 groups during the National Day holiday, with an average of about five travelers per group. Families and friends made up a significant share of customers choosing eight- to 10-day itineraries. The company's packages combine transport and accommodation with optional experiences such as wine tasting, boat trips, local dining and cultural activities, allowing travelers to tailor their spending to their interests. FACTORS BEHIND TRAVEL BOOM The most immediate factor behind the surge in long-haul travel was more time off than usual this year, making trips involving long flights and multiple destinations more feasible. Gu Sui, general manager of China Southern Airlines' Spain office, said taking extra days off around public holidays had spread departures over a longer period, easing congestion during the traditional peak travel period. Longer stays also allow travelers to spread the cost of intercontinental travel over more days of sightseeing and leisure, making distant destinations more worthwhile. Improved air connectivity was another factor. Aviation consultancy CAPA said in an April analysis that capacity between China and Western Europe had surpassed 2019 levels, driven by Chinese airlines. As of early October, about 85 weekly nonstop passenger flights connected Germany with destinations on the Chinese mainland, with Frankfurt accounting for roughly two-thirds of the total. This year's new services and increased frequencies included Air China's Frankfurt-Beijing Daxing route and China Southern's Guangzhou-Urumqi-Frankfurt service, as well as more frequent flights between Frankfurt and Shanghai. In Croatia, Air China's new Beijing-Bucharest-Zagreb service opened another gateway for Chinese visitors. Zagreb recorded a 7 percent year-on-year increase in Chinese arrivals and an 8 percent rise in their overnight stays in September, according to Martina Bienenfeld, director of the Zagreb Tourist Board. "This is a very promising start, especially considering that only a few weeks have passed since the new route was established," she said. European destinations are also working to turn improved connectivity into deeper engagement with Chinese visitors. One example is the "More than 88 hours in Madrid" campaign, which encourages extended stays in the Spanish capital. The Polish Tourism Organisation's 2026 action plan includes updating a WeChat-based guide for independent travelers with interactive maps and attraction information, as well as pilot training and certification programs to help hotels, restaurants and attractions better serve Chinese guests. The Zagreb Tourist Board maintains a presence in Beijing and Shanghai. It recently promoted the Croatian capital's year-round events and cuisine in Beijing. Zagreb is also showcasing an art installation at the Shanghai International Light Festival through mid-October, as the two cities mark 46 years of sister-city ties. "All these activities, combined with the new air link, are vital components of our long-term strategy to position Zagreb in the Chinese market," said Bienenfeld. (Video reporters: Ma Ruxuan, Jiao Qian, Liu Haodong, Sun Xinjing, Yang Yating and He Canling; Video editors: Zhang Yueyuan, Luo Hui and Wang Han) ■

item.title: Last Voices of the Long Marchers
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
In commemoration of the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, Xinhua presents this video, bringing to life the voices and memories of the Red Army veterans who lived through it. Though they have passed away, their voices live on. Through their memories, we revisit a journey marked by unimaginable hardship, sacrifice, and unwavering faith. From fierce battles to snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, their stories bring the Long March to life and remind us of a spirit that continues to echo across generations.■

item.title: U.S. needs to handle Taiwan question prudently: FM spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- The U.S. needs to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, handle the Taiwan question prudently, and take concrete actions to uphold the overall China-U.S. relations and peace and stability in the region, a foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday. Spokesperson Mao Ning told a regular press briefing after the U.S. State Department last week said China's maritime activities off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilizing." "China has on multiple occasions made clear its position on this," said Mao, adding that China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in waters east of the Taiwan island. It is fully within China's sovereign rights and jurisdiction, therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters. "The party that instigates troubles and disrupts stability in this part of waters has never been the Chinese side," Mao emphasized, saying that the Taiwan question is China's internal affair that brooks no external interference. ■

item.title: China to cut NEV export tax rebate for high-quality auto industry growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- China announced on Monday that it will cut the value-added tax (VAT) export rebate rate for new energy vehicles (NEVs) to 9 percent from 13 percent starting April 1, 2027. VAT export rebates for e-cigarette devices and related products will be scrapped from the same date, according to a statement jointly issued by the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration. Export consumption tax policies for products subject to the tax will remain unchanged, with existing tax refund or exemption arrangements continuing to apply, the statement said. The adjustment comes as China has continued to optimize export tax rebate policies. The country scrapped VAT export rebates for photovoltaic products from April 1, 2026, while cutting the rebate rate for battery products to 6 percent from 9 percent on the same date. The rebates for battery products will be eliminated from Jan. 1, 2027. China is the world's largest market for NEVs, a category that includes battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles. The sector has expanded rapidly in recent years, with automakers increasingly looking to overseas markets for growth. Luo Zhiheng, chief economist at Yuekai Securities, told business news network Yicai that cutting export tax rebates can, to some extent, reduce rat race competition and encourage companies to shift from low-price competition to technology and brand-based competition. "China's NEVs are highly competitive internationally. Against the backdrop of tight global supplies of traditional energy, NEVs have met the needs of residents in Europe and the United States. Even with a partial rebate cut, they can retain sufficient competitiveness," Luo said. "Objectively, this also plays a positive role in stabilizing the macro tax burden and can better support the development of domestic demand." During the January-September period, China's auto exports totaled 8.205 million units, including over 4 million NEVs, more than double the level a year earlier, according to the latest data. "Despite a complex and severe external environment, exports have continued to grow rapidly, demonstrating strong resilience, while domestic new growth drivers are being steadily unleashed and the share of NEV sales is rising steadily," said Chen Shihua, deputy secretary-general of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, the industry is expected to maintain steady operation, Chen said. ■

item.title: Xi Focus: Turning China's innovation moments into lasting momentum
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- In June 2024, China's Chang'e-6 probe brought back humanity's first samples ever retrieved from the far side of the moon, an achievement hailed by global media as historic. Seven months later, DeepSeek's R1 reasoning model drew worldwide attention to China's advances in artificial intelligence (AI), with a Silicon Valley venture capitalist calling it AI's "Sputnik moment." The wave of innovation milestones carried into 2026. In March, China approved the market launch of an invasive brain-computer interface medical device by a Chinese company, indicating that the device has now entered the phase of clinical application. Last week, the journal Nature published a research article reporting that Chinese scientists had developed a nuclear clock capable of stable operation, marking a breakthrough in ultra-precise time measurement with potential applications in satellite navigation and deep-space exploration. How to transform breakthroughs in individual fields into lasting gains in productivity across the economy? China has made headway in this regard, as it is pursuing "new quality productive forces," an innovation-centered major task put forward by President Xi Jinping. During an inspection tour of northeast China's Heilongjiang Province in September 2023, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, brought the concept of new quality productive forces to the public's attention, calling for better integration of sci-tech innovation resources and the development of strategic emerging and future industries. At the Central Economic Work Conference that December, Xi urged efforts to drive industrial innovation through sci-tech innovation, particularly by leveraging disruptive and cutting-edge technologies to foster new industries, new models and new growth drivers, and to develop new quality productive forces. The policy drive stepped up on Oct. 9, when the CPC Central Committee and the State Council issued guidelines setting out 19 key measures to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces. INNOVATE TO WIN THE FUTURE "Innovation drives development and innovation shapes the future," Xi has stressed. Shifting toward innovation-driven growth is imperative for China. The country has built a complete industrial system covering all industrial categories in the United Nations classification, yet it is still grappling with major pressures from demographic shifts to resource and environment constraints. The fact that some of its key technologies remain dependent on other countries, along with intensifying technological revolution and competition, adds urgency to this shift. Xi's expositions on this concept have provided guidance for the country's high-quality development as well as for Chinese modernization. At a group study session of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee in January 2024, Xi said "developing new quality productive forces is an intrinsic requirement and an important focus of promoting high-quality development." With innovation playing the leading role, new quality productive forces mean advanced productivity that is freed from traditional economic growth mode and productivity development paths, features high-tech, high efficiency and high quality, and comes in line with the new development philosophy, said Xi. From quantum technology and new energy to AI and future industries, sci-tech innovation has been a recurring focus of the Political Bureau's group study sessions in recent years. The emphasis on breaking new ground echoes a long-standing idea in Chinese philosophy. At a meeting on cultural inheritance and development in June 2023, Xi identified innovation as one of the five defining characteristics of Chinese civilization. Acutely aware of what matters for an economy with a vast industrial base, Xi has stressed that developing new quality productive forces "does not mean neglecting or abandoning traditional industries." He also stressed that developing new quality productive forces should be tailored to local conditions, warning against both a headlong rush into new industries and the neglect of traditional industrial strengths. The guidelines issued on Oct. 9 align with this approach, calling for measures tailored to local conditions and for "establishing the new before abolishing the old." An official with the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) said these principles are intended to correct problems seen in practice, including investment and planning divorced from reality, a rush into emerging and future industries, and neglect of upgrading traditional industries. FROM DISCOVERY TO PRODUCTIVITY The crucial link is turning knowledge into application. Addressing a national science and technology gathering in Beijing in July 2026, Xi summed up the relationship: sci-tech innovation should highlight an application-oriented approach, while industrial innovation should raise scientific questions. The brain-computer interface device approved in March illustrates how this works in practice. By decoding neural signals and transmitting commands to a pneumatic glove, it helps eligible patients with cervical spinal cord injuries perform grasping movements. Its market approval marks an important step toward wider clinical use. In manufacturing, the demand for better products can itself steer research. At Yangquan Valve Co., Ltd., a century-old manufacturer in north China's Shanxi Province, engineers have developed ball valves for hydrogen pipelines, opening possibilities beyond its traditional products. During a visit to the factory in July 2025, Xi emphasized responding to market demand and using technological innovation to breathe new life into traditional industries. During a November 2025 visit to south China's Guangdong Province, Xi reviewed progress in integrating sci-tech innovation with industrial innovation, and called for the building of an internationally competitive modern industrial system. He also stressed the need to accelerate indigenous innovation, vigorously support the adoption of homegrown innovative products, and foster a favorable environment for their application. China's large market, extensive supply chains and strong research capacity create opportunities to turn scientific advances into industrial applications. In Guangdong, a manufacturing powerhouse, the value added of the province's 20 major industrial clusters accounted for 31.7 percent of its GDP in 2025. In east China's Anhui Province, an expanding network of vehicle manufacturers and suppliers brings together batteries, chips, materials and vehicle assembly, making it possible to build an entire new energy vehicle without leaving the province. The broader shift is visible in national figures. In August 2026, value added by high-tech manufacturing enterprises above the designated size rose 16.7 percent year on year, compared with a 5.2 percent increase for industrial enterprises above the designated size overall. The green transition offers another marker: renewable energy accounted for 73.9 percent of all newly installed power generation capacity in the first half of 2026, according to the National Energy Administration. These changes show the scale of the transformation under way. Making the gains durable, however, requires more than successful products or fast-growing sectors. It requires an innovation system that can generate, test, finance, and spread successive rounds of advances. SUSTAINING INNOVATION, SHARING OPPORTUNITIES Xi has repeatedly focused on what happens between an invention and its wider adoption. During a November 2024 visit to the Wuhan Institute of Industrial Innovation and Development in central China's Hubei Province, he asked about development timelines, cost reductions, international competitiveness and cooperation with enterprises -- practical questions about how technology reaches the market. There is also a longer horizon. Xi has emphasized basic research, which may not yield immediate commercial returns but provides the discoveries on which future industries depend. At a symposium on basic research in Shanghai in April 2026, Xi said, "We must seize opportunities, rise to challenges, put basic research high on the agenda, advance it with sustained commitment, and strive for continuous achievements." China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) places the development of new quality productive forces and greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology among its strategic priorities. Liu Zhenzhong, a researcher at the Institute of Industrial and Technological Economics of the NDRC, noted that transformative technologies are changing how innovation is organized and how resources are allocated. Institutional reform, he said, is therefore needed to clear barriers to development. Xi has charted a practical path for empowering new quality productive forces through reform. He called for efforts to deepen reform of economic and sci-tech systems to "remove bottlenecks and blockages that constrain the development of new quality productive forces." He also urged establishing a high-standard market system and developing new ways to allocate production factors. Reform efforts include guidelines issued in April 2026 to deepen reform of the ChiNext board of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, the country's Nasdaq-style board of growth enterprises; an initiative launched in 2024 to promote mutual recognition of data products across trading platforms; and measures aimed at improving market-access rules. Xi has also emphasized that innovation is not confined within national borders. At the second session of the 32nd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in November 2025, he stressed digital, smart and green development and called on Asia-Pacific economies to "move faster to nurture and promote new quality productive forces." He advocated deeper cooperation on open-source technologies and an open, competitive ecosystem for innovation. The core technology behind the signature substrate product of Austrian semiconductor materials company AT&S was first commercialized in southwest China's Chongqing Municipality and has since been refined there. CEO Michael Mertin said China has long made it a priority to train scientists and engineers, and the new generation of Chinese engineers "not only possesses outstanding mathematical skills but is also increasingly creative." "In today's digital age, no company, city or country can innovate in isolation," Mertin said. "High-tech progress depends on trusted global networks, cross-border collaboration, and the exchange of talent, expertise and ideas." In the latest signal of openness and cooperation, the new guidelines call for allocating advanced factors of production globally, building global networks for innovation cooperation, and establishing efficient, convenient and secure mechanisms for cross-border data flows. "The more complex the international environment, the more we should be open-minded and engage with the world. We should determine the right balance between opening up and security, and achieve greater strength and self-reliance in science and technology through international cooperation," Xi once said. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Madise on assuming Estonian presidency
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday extended congratulations to Ulle Madise on her assumption of office as president of Estonia. Xi said that China and Estonia enjoy a traditional friendship and that bilateral relations have maintained steady development in recent years, with continued progress in exchanges and cooperation across various fields, bringing benefits to the two peoples. Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Estonia relations and stands ready to work with President Madise to take the 35th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries this year as an opportunity to enhance political mutual trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and continuously enrich the contemporary connotations of bilateral relations. ■

item.title: Xi, Papua New Guinea's governor-general exchange congratulations over 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Bob Dadae, governor-general of Papua New Guinea, on Monday exchanged congratulations on the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. In his message, Xi noted that Papua New Guinea is a good friend, good partner and good brother of China in the Pacific island region. Over the past 50 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in mutually beneficial cooperation, and expanded people-to-people exchanges, raising bilateral relations to new heights, Xi said. These achievements have benefited the two peoples and injected strong impetus into building a China-Pacific Island countries community with a shared future, said Xi. Noting that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Papua New Guinea relations, Xi said that he stands ready to work with Dadae to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, strengthen exchanges and cooperation across various fields, and elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea to a new level, so as to deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. For his part, Dadae said that over the past 50 years, bilateral relations have made significant progress, benefiting both countries and their peoples. Papua New Guinea cherishes the longstanding friendship with China, firmly upholds the one-China principle, and looks forward to taking the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further deepen and advance bilateral relations, he said. On the same day, Chinese Premier Li Qiang also exchanged congratulations with Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape. China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and advance the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea, Li said in the message. For his part, Marape said that the Papua New Guinean government highly appreciates China's significant contributions to the country's economic and social development. Papua New Guinea will continue to uphold the one-China principle it has long adhered to, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation with China across various fields and advance the development of the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries, said Marape. ■
